title: Fix the Deployment
description: An inventory API never comes up on Kubernetes. Find and fix the bugs in its Deployment, Service and ConfigMap. CI grades your PR on a kind cluster.
summary: An inventory API never comes up on Kubernetes. Find and fix the bugs in its Deployment, Service and ConfigMap until the rollout finishes and the Service answers.
situation: The inventory API was moved to Kubernetes on Friday. On Monday it is still not serving: the rollout never finishes, and the few times a pod looked healthy, nothing answered behind the Service. The person who wrote the manifests is on holiday.

The app itself is fine. It reads the store name from STORE_NAME and refuses to start without it, listens on port 8080, answers ok on GET /healthz and JSON with the store's stock on GET /. The manifests in k8s/ are where the bugs are, and there is more than one.
task: The inventory-api Deployment rolls out with 2 of 2 replicas ready.
The inventory-api Service routes to the pods.
GET / on port 80 of the Service answers HTTP 200 for the store named in the ConfigMap.
The pods stay up without restarts.
Keep the image and its entrypoint, the 2 replicas, both HTTP probes, STORE_NAME from a ConfigMap, and the security settings: the namespace enforces Pod Security restricted.

checks.name: The manifests apply
checks.description: The files in k8s/ parse and apply, and only define the inventory-api Deployment and Service plus ConfigMaps. The image, the 2 replicas and both HTTP probes stay in place, STORE_NAME comes from a ConfigMap, and the pods meet Pod Security restricted (no root, no privileged mode, no host namespaces or host paths). Nothing is applied until these checks pass.

checks.name: The rollout finishes
checks.description: kubectl rollout status for deployment/inventory-api succeeds within 120 seconds, with 2 of 2 replicas ready.

checks.name: The Service has endpoints
checks.description: The inventory-api Service routes to at least one ready pod.

checks.name: The Service answers
checks.description: GET / on port 80 of the Service's cluster IP answers HTTP 200 with the store name from the ConfigMap.

checks.name: The pods stay up
checks.description: 30 seconds after the other checks: the URLs both probes call answer 2xx without a redirect, 2 of 2 replicas are still ready, and no container restarted.

hints.title: Start where Kubernetes tells you
hints.body: kubectl get pods, then kubectl describe pod and read the Events at the bottom. kubectl logs shows what the app printed before it stopped.

hints.title: A pod that runs but is never ready
hints.body: Something decides when a pod is ready. Ask the app what it actually serves: port-forward to the Deployment and curl the paths the probes use.

hints.title: Ready pods, but the Service does not answer
hints.body: kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=inventory-api shows which pods the Service sends traffic to, and on which port. Compare the Service with the pods it should select.

localTest.intro: From the challenge folder, with Docker, kind and kubectl:
localTest.commands:
kind create cluster --name inventory
docker build -t devops-daily/inventory-api:1.0 app/
kind load docker-image devops-daily/inventory-api:1.0 --name inventory
kubectl create namespace challenge
kubectl label namespace challenge pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted
kubectl apply -n challenge -f k8s/
kubectl -n challenge rollout status deployment/inventory-api --timeout=120s
kind delete cluster --name inventory
